headline: WHEAT BREAKS 3.4%; SEPTEMBER WASDE SETUP BEGINS
subheadline: Chicago wheat had its biggest single-session drop in weeks; corn and beans drift lower into the Labor Day weekend with harvest pressure building.
lead: Wheat closed at $7.16, off 25 cents, its biggest one-day drop in several weeks, and the move is telling you the funds found a reason to step out before the long weekend. Corn settled $5.12, beans $12.94, both off small. The September WASDE on the 11th is now the first real reset since USDA's August yield cuts landed below expectations.
the_takeaway: Wheat funds stepped out hard; hold unpriced corn through the WASDE, not past it.
teaser: Wheat breaks 25 cents, funds exit before the holiday. Corn and beans drift. The WASDE is next.

one_number.unit: year-over-year rise in US beef export value, July
one_number.context: USDA data out today shows beef export value rose 6% in July year-over-year while pork fell on PRV-related technical barriers. Demand is holding on the beef side even as the Cargill lockout constrains processing capacity.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called corn down toward $4.99. Corn closed $5.12 today, up from yesterday's $5.075 settle -- nowhere near the target.
yesterdays_call.note: Miss. Harvest pressure is real but hasn't been enough; $4.99 needs a weather-free WASDE confirmation the funds don't have yet.

sections.title: WHEAT BREAKS; CORN DRIFTS
sections.body:
- Chicago wheat fell 25 cents to **$7.16**, its biggest session drop in several weeks, with no fresh USDA catalyst and the funds clearly rotating out before the three-day weekend.
- Corn gave back 3.5 cents to $5.12 nearby; the FAO Food Price Index rising in August on Middle East conflict and Black Sea logistics didn't give the board enough to work with against harvest-pressure selling.
- December corn at $5.37 is still above the August 12 report-day close of $4.78, but every week of harvest progress that arrives without a weather scare takes a little air out of that premium.
sections.catalyst: Fund liquidation pre-holiday weekend; no fresh USDA data; FAO August food price rise insufficient to offset selling.
sections.bottom_line: Wheat's exit was the funds, not the fundamentals; the WASDE on the 11th resets the story.
sections.farmer_action: If you have unpriced December corn, hold through the September 11 WASDE; selling into Friday afternoon fund liquidation is not the window.
sections.vs_yesterday: Corn: yesterday's export-sales decision point passed; price drifted lower, not resolved.

sections.title: BEANS AND MEAL SPLIT
sections.body:
- Nearby soybeans settled $12.94, off 14 cents, still near the top of the 52-week range at 96% from the low.
- Soybean oil dropped 3.3% to **$68.74**, giving back ground from this week's gains as the crush margin story resets; meal barely moved, up a dime to $345.30, sitting at a fresh 52-week high.
- China's $17 billion annual US ag purchase commitment (May 18 deal, through 2028) continues to show up as periodic confirmed sales, but the buy-the-rumor pattern is keeping November beans from running past $13.10.
sections.catalyst: Soybean oil drop offsets meal strength; China purchase cadence ongoing without fresh confirmed sale today.
sections.bottom_line: Meal at a 52-week high is the real bean story; oil's pullback is the drag.

sections.title: CATTLE HOLDS; BEEF EXPORTS FIRM
sections.body:
- Live cattle settled $213.15, off half a percent, with the Cargill multi-plant lockout ongoing since May 19 still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity.
- Feeders gave back less, settling $325.20, down 0.2%; the screwworm-driven closure of Mexican feeder cattle imports, with the first phased port reopening set for Aug 24 at Douglas, AZ, is now in the market's rearview for pricing purposes.
- The beef export value print rising 6% in July year-over-year is the one clean piece of demand data that says the buyer is patient, not gone.
sections.catalyst: Beef export value +6% year-over-year in July (USDA data, reported today); packer lockout supply constraint ongoing.
sections.bottom_line: Cattle holding $213 with export demand firm; processing constraint, not cattle numbers, is still the binding story.
sections.vs_yesterday: Cattle: packer margin story intact; no new break in either direction.

sections.title: DIESEL TIGHTENS; CRUDE EASES
sections.body:
- WTI crude settled $91.22, off 0.9%; the Iran-Hormuz cycle, a July re-escalation that has since cooled with the premium deflating again into August, is not the driver today.
- Diesel crack spreads remain elevated and are the real input-cost story for fall fieldwork; refined products, not crude, have been pushing Brent toward $95 per today's trade reporting.
- Illinois 2027 crop budgets flagged higher fuel and fertilizer costs as a projected headwind even as improved crop pricing offsets some of it.
sections.catalyst: Diesel crack spreads tightening on middle distillate supply; EIA and trade press confirm elevated crack spreads Friday.
sections.bottom_line: Crude eases but diesel stays tight; fall fieldwork cost is a diesel story, not a crude story.

outside_the_pit.title: Trump Signs Executive Orders Targeting Cattle Industry Support
outside_the_pit.body: New executive orders out Friday aim to expand market access for US meat producers and signal renewed White House engagement with the cattle sector. Producers watching packer concentration and the ongoing Cargill lockout should note whether any order touches processing rules or import authority.

outside_the_pit.title: USDA Piloting Satellite and Tech Upgrades for Crop Reports
outside_the_pit.body: Secretary Rollins confirmed Tuesday that USDA is launching a satellite-and-tech pilot to sharpen acreage and yield estimates, starting with crop progress methodology. If it works, it narrows the gap between USDA and private estimates like Pro Farmer's, which matters for how the market trades every monthly WASDE.

weekly_thread.question: Will this week's Crop Progress rating confirm the August yield cuts or add a weather premium back into corn and beans?
weekly_thread.status_text: Monday's crop progress confirmed the Belt on pace with no weather premium added; the September WASDE on Sept 11 at 11 AM CT now carries that question forward.

the_more_you_know.title: Meal at a 52-week high while oil falls: what the split says
the_more_you_know.body: Soybean meal sitting at a 52-week high while soybean oil drops 3.3% in a session tells you crush demand is being driven by protein, not fat. That keeps crush margins supported even as biofuel headwinds pressure oil. For producers watching basis, a protein-led crush is more durable than an oil-led one.

watch_list.desc: Weekly export sales. Corn below 600K MT or soybeans below 500K MT removes the demand leg from the post-WASDE story.
September WASDE. Corn yield above 181 bu/acre confirms the big-crop thesis; below 180 reopens the August break. Soybean carryout above 330M bu is bearish for November beans.
USDA Crop Progress. Corn harvest above 10% nationally starts pricing harvest pressure; any weather-related rating decline adds premium back.
Markets reopen after Labor Day weekend. Watch for overnight positioning reset, especially in wheat after today's fund exit.

daily_quote.text: Sell down to the sleeping point.
